mainTopic: What is included in a sale (a donkey's vessels, accessories, an animal's young, a container's contents), followed by רבי יוחנן's lesson about making 'the account of the world.'
overview: The amud continues the question of whether a donkey's vessels are sold with it when they are on the donkey. רבינא tries to prove it from the wagon-and-mules case. The גמרא pushes back using the ship משנה and concludes that the תנא teaches each ruling on its own, so no proof works. אביי then lists six תנאים who all hold that a sale includes an item's accessories, and the גמרא shows the source for each one. רבא explains why, according to רבי יהודה, 'this donkey of yours' includes the vessels but 'is the donkey yours?' does not. A new משנה teaches that a sold donkey comes with its foal but a cow does not come with its calf, and that containers like a cistern or a beehive are sold with what is inside them. רב פפא explains the donkey-cow difference: the seller said 'nursing,' and only a cow's milk has value. The amud closes with רבי יוחנן's lesson on the פסוקים about חשבון. A wise person weighs the true account of his deeds, while those who follow their desires, the arrogant, and the רשע who denies judgment will face it. This lesson continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה was talking about a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away an earlier attempted proof. It says רבי יהודה's statement was about a separate matter, not a disagreement on the same case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking about a different matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects an earlier attempt to answer the question from רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. It says he was simply talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attempted proof assumed that the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה argue about vessels that are on the donkey. The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה is adding a separate case, so we cannot learn what the תנא קמא holds about that case. The question stays open.

phrases.english: He was speaking of a different matter.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה from the משנה. He isn't arguing about the same case; he is adding a new one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מלתא אחריתי קאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier attempted proof from רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempted proof from רבי יהודה's words in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed that רבי יהודה and the תנא קמא are arguing about the same case.

steps.title: רבינא brings the story of the wagon and the mules
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רב אשי about a ברייתא saying the mules are sold with the wagon. That seems to contradict our משנה. רבי אבהו settled it by explaining the ברייתא as speaking about mules that are tied to the wagon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear. The משנה says that if someone sold a wagon, he has not sold the mules. But רב תחליפא from ארץ ישראל taught before רבי אבהו that if someone sold a wagon, he has sold the mules. רבי אבהו asked him: But we learned in the משנה that he has not sold them! רב תחליפא asked: Should I erase my teaching? רבי אבהו answered: No. Explain your ברייתא as talking about mules that are tied to the wagon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא begins a new attempt to answer the question about the donkey. He first tells a story about the wagon and the mules, which sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the mules are not sold, and the ברייתא says they are. רבי אבהו does not throw out the ברייתא. He resolves the clash by saying the ברייתא speaks about mules that are tied to the wagon, which are sold along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
Explain it, interpret it as speaking about

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different texts here. The משנה says the mules are not sold, and the ברייתא of רב תחליפא says they are sold. Keep track of which is which.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַקָּרוֹן – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַפְּרָדוֹת.
phrases.english: If one sold the wagon, he has not sold the mules.
And Rav Tachlifa from the West taught
before Rabbi Abbahu:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַקָּרוֹן – מָכַר אֶת הַפְּרָדוֹת.
phrases.english: If one sold the wagon, he has sold the mules.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא אֲנַן ״לֹא מָכַר״ תְּנַן!
phrases.english: And he said to him: But we learned "he has not sold"!
And he said to him: Should I erase it?
And he said to him: No,
explain your ברייתא as speaking of when they are fastened to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבינא לרב אשי תא שמע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier proof failed, so רבינא opens a new attempt to answer the question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether vessels that are on the donkey are sold with it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wagon משנה, the ברייתא of רב תחליפא, and רבי אבהו's explanation of the ברייתא.

steps.title: So the donkey case must be about vessels that are not on it
steps.stepSummary: From רבי אבהו's answer we learn that the wagon משנה speaks about mules that are not tied. The donkey משנה, which comes after it, should then also speak about vessels that are not on the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that our משנה speaks about mules that are not tied to the wagon. Since the earlier clause speaks about a case where they are not attached, the later clause about the donkey must also speak about vessels that are not on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא now draws the proof from the story. Both the wagon ruling and the donkey ruling deal with things that are not attached. So when the vessels are on the donkey, they would be sold with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's answer tells us that the wagon משנה speaks about mules that are not tied. רבינא assumes that the clauses of the משנה are set up the same way. So the donkey ruling ("the vessels are not sold") also speaks only about vessels that are not on the donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; we can learn from this
They are still on it (the vessels are on the donkey)

phrases.english: By inference, our משנה is speaking of when they are not fastened to it;
and since the first clause is about when they are not on it,
phrases.notes: The "first clause" is the wagon ruling. The "later clause" is our donkey ruling.

phrases.english: the latter clause too is about when they are not on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מכלל דמתניתין בשאין אדוקים בו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof from the wagon story.
steps.raayaObject: That vessels on the donkey are sold with it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wagon משנה as רבי אבהו explained it, together with the idea that the clauses of a משנה follow the same setup.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof depends on one idea: the earlier and later rulings of the משנה are set up in the same kind of case.

steps.title: The ship case points the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the ship משנה. There, the merchandise is not sold even though it is inside the ship. By the same logic, the donkey ruling would speak about vessels that are on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Look at the earlier clause about the ship: he has not sold the slaves or the אנתיקי. We asked what אנתיקי means, and רב פפא said it is the merchandise inside the ship. Since that clause speaks about things that are on the ship, the later clause should also speak about vessels that are on the donkey!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבינא's proof. It uses his own method, comparing the clauses, with a different earlier clause, and gets the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ship's merchandise is inside the ship, yet it is not sold. If we compare clauses, the donkey ruling would speak about vessels that are on the donkey and say they are not sold. Since comparing clauses can give either answer, the method proves nothing.

phrases.english: On the contrary, say the first clause:
phrases.notes: Here the "first clause" is the earlier משנה about selling a ship.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת הָעֲבָדִים
phrases.english: but he has not sold the slaves
nor the antikei.
And we said: What is "antikei"?
Rav Pappa said: The merchandise that is inside it.
And since the first clause is about when they are on it,
the latter clause too is about when they are on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אדרבה אימא רישא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same clause-comparing method to reach the opposite result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבינא's proof from the wagon clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Comparing clauses gives opposite results depending on which earlier clause you pick, so it is not a reliable proof.

steps.title: Each ruling of the משנה stands on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the תנא taught each ruling separately. We cannot learn the setup of one case from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא teaches each matter on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the discussion. The rulings in this list are separate, so the donkey question cannot be answered by comparing it to the other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 4 showed that the clause-comparing method gives opposite answers. So the גמרא drops the assumption that the clauses share one setup. The proof falls away, and the question about vessels on the donkey is not settled here.
steps.whatToRemember: Comparing clauses only works if they are all set in the same kind of case. Here the תנא teaches each ruling on its own, so no proof can be drawn, and the donkey question stays open.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common tool in the גמרא for knocking down a proof that is based on comparing different clauses of a משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, the תנא teaches matter by matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא תנא מילי מילי קתני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the clash between steps 3 and 4 by giving up the clause-comparison approach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The clauses of the משנה are separate rulings, so רבינא's proof does not work.

steps.title: Six תנאים who hold that a sale includes the accessories
steps.stepSummary: אביי lists six תנאים who all hold that when a person sells an item, he also sells all of its accessories.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A memory aid: זגם, נסן.] אביי said: רבי אליעזר, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי מאיר, רבי נתן, סומכוס and נחום המדי all hold the same thing. When a person sells something, he sells it together with everything used with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a general rule and names six תנאים who share it. In the next step the גמרא will show where each of them says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה has נחום המדי saying that the donkey's vessels are sold with the donkey. אביי shows that this is part of a wider view held by several תנאים. They all treat an item's accessories as part of the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid. Here it is made from letters of the תנאים's names.
Its accessories, the things used together with it
They hold, this is their opinion

phrases.english: [A memory aid: Z-G-M, N-S-N]
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for a name in the list: אליעזר, גמליאל, מאיר, נתן, סומכוס, נחום.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and Rabbi Meir,
and Rabbi Natan, and Sumakhos, and Nachum the Mede –
all of them hold:
when a person sells something,
he sells it and all its accessories.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְרַבִּי נָתָן, וְסוֹמְכוֹס, וְנַחוּם הַמָּדִי – כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of how the wagon, donkey and ship cases are set up, אביי steps back and names a group of תנאים who share one view about selling accessories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a person sells an item, he also sells all of its accessories. Six named תנאים hold this.

steps.title: Where each of the six תנאים says this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source for each name on אביי's list, showing that each one includes the accessories in a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר: a משנה says that one who sells an olive press has also sold the beam. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a משנה says that one who sells a city has also sold the city guard. רבי מאיר: a ברייתא says that one who sells a vineyard has also sold the vineyard's tools. רבי נתן and סומכוס: they say this about the small boats of a ship. נחום המדי: this is what we said in our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי's list. It points to a case for each תנא where he says the extra items go along with the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source involves something separate from the main item: a beam, a guard, tools, small boats, or a donkey's vessels. In every case, the תנא includes it in the sale. This is why they can all be grouped under one rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The heavy beam used to press the olives
The small boats that belong to a ship
As we learned in a משנה / as it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer – as we learned in a mishna,
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת בֵּית הַבַּד – מָכַר אֶת הַקּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: one who sells an olive press has sold the beam.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel – as we learned in a mishna,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הָעִיר – מָכַר אֶת הַסַּנְטֵר.
phrases.english: one who sells a city has sold the guard.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר – דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir – as it is taught in a baraita, Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַכֶּרֶם – מָכַר תַּשְׁמִישֵׁי הַכֶּרֶם.
phrases.english: if he sold the vineyard, he sold the vineyard's accessories.
Rabbi Natan and Sumakhos – the small boats of the ship.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier discussion of selling a ship, where these two include the small boats in the sale.

phrases.english: Nachum the Mede – that which we said.
phrases.notes: He means our משנה, where נחום המדי says the donkey's vessels are sold with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step brings the sources behind each name in אביי's list.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that all six תנאים hold that a sale includes the accessories
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משניות about the olive press and the city, a ברייתא about the vineyard, the earlier discussion of the ship's small boats, and our donkey משנה
steps.whatToRemember: Six תנאים share one view: a sale includes the item's accessories. They are רבי אליעזר (the beam), רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (the city guard), רבי מאיר (the vineyard's tools), רבי נתן and סומכוס (the ship's small boats), and נחום המדי (the donkey's vessels).

steps.title: Why do the two wordings in רבי יהודה's ruling differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling and asks what the difference is between "this donkey of yours" and "is the donkey yours?"
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: sometimes the vessels are sold, and so on. What is different about "this donkey of yours", and what is different about "is the donkey yours?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה. It asks why two wordings that sound so alike lead to different results. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says that if the buyer said "this donkey of yours," the vessels are sold. If he said "is the donkey yours?" they are not. In both cases the buyer is talking about the same donkey, so the גמרא wants to know what makes the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks why two cases have different results.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: פְּעָמִים מְכוּרִין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: sometimes they are sold, etc.
phrases.notes: "They" means the donkey's vessels. The rest of the משנה says when they are sold and when they are not.

phrases.english: What is different about "this donkey of yours,"
and what is different about "is the donkey yours?"

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא ״חֲמוֹרְךָ זוֹ״, וּמַאי שְׁנָא ״חֲמוֹרְךָ הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the list of תנאים, the גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה, רבי יהודה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why "this donkey of yours" includes the vessels while "is the donkey yours?" does not

steps.title: רבא: the extra word "this" points to the vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that "this donkey of yours" adds the word "this," which points to the vessels. "Is the donkey yours?" only checks whether the seller owns the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: when the buyer says "this donkey of yours," he already knows the donkey belongs to the seller. So when he adds the word "this," he is saying it because of the vessels. When he says "is the donkey yours?", he does not know whether the donkey belongs to him. This is what he means: Is the donkey yours, so that you can sell it to me?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by reading each wording closely. Each wording shows what the buyer had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In "this donkey of yours," the buyer already knows who owns the donkey. So the extra word "this" must be pointing at the donkey as it stands, loaded with its vessels, and the vessels are included. In "is the donkey yours?" the buyer is only checking that the seller can sell it, so he is asking about the donkey alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Its vessels, the gear loaded on the donkey
That you can sell it to me

phrases.english: Rava said: "this donkey of yours" –
he knows that the donkey is his,
and that which he said to him: "this" –
he says it to him because of its vessels.
"Is the donkey yours" –
means he does not know that the donkey is his,
and this is what he is saying to him:
Is the donkey yours – so that you can sell it to me?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: ״חֲמוֹרְךָ זוֹ״ – יָדַע דַּחֲמָרָא דִידֵיהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step answers the question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "This donkey of yours" adds the word "this," which points to the vessels, so they are sold. "Is the donkey yours?" only asks about ownership, so only the donkey is sold.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the buyer's exact words decide the sale. The word "זוֹ" ("this") points to the vessels on the donkey, so they are included. Asking "is it yours?" only checks who owns the donkey, so the vessels are not included.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two wordings. The one with "זוֹ" ("this donkey of yours") is the one that includes the vessels. The question "is the donkey yours?" is about the donkey alone.

steps.title: New משנה: which sales include the young or the contents
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a sold donkey includes its foal but a sold cow does not include its calf. A dunghill, a cistern, a beehive and a dovecote are sold together with their contents.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sells a donkey, the foal goes with it. If he sells a cow, the calf does not go with it. If he sells a dunghill, the manure goes with it. If he sells a cistern, the water goes with it. If he sells a beehive, the bees go with it. If he sells a dovecote, the doves go with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists sales and tells us what is automatically included in each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases look alike, a donkey and a cow, but they get opposite rulings, and the גמרא will soon ask why. The other four cases follow one pattern: the container is sold together with what is inside it.

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר – מָכַר אֶת הַסְּיָח.
phrases.english: One who sells the donkey has sold the foal.

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַפָּרָה – לֹא מָכַר אֶת בְּנָהּ.
phrases.english: If he sold the cow, he has not sold its young.
If he sold a dunghill, he has sold its manure.
If he sold a cistern, he has sold its water.
If he sold a beehive, he has sold the bees.
If he sold a dovecote, he has sold the doves.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר מָכַר אֶת הַסְּיָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier discussion was about the accessories of a sold item, and this משנה moves to a sold animal's young and a container's contents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A donkey is sold with its foal, but a cow is not sold with its calf. A dunghill, a cistern, a beehive and a dovecote are sold with their contents.

steps.title: How can the donkey and the cow be different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means. If the seller said 'it and its young,' the calf should also be sold. If he did not say it, the foal should not be sold either.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If the seller said 'the animal and its young,' then even a cow should come with its calf. If he did not say 'the animal and its young,' then even a donkey should not come with its foal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from both sides. It cannot find any case where the donkey and the cow would come out differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either the seller said the words 'it and its young' or he did not. In both cases the two animals should get the same ruling, so the משנה's split between them needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?

phrases.english: Gemara:
What are the circumstances?
If he said to him: 'It and its young,'
then even a cow and its young should also be sold!
If he did not say to him 'it and its young,'
then even a donkey should not be sold with its foal!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה just quoted, asking what case would make the donkey and the cow different.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's different rulings for the donkey and the cow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. Whether or not the seller said 'it and its young,' both animals should get the same ruling.

steps.title: רב פפא: the seller said 'a nursing animal'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the seller said 'I am selling you a nursing donkey' or 'a nursing cow.' For a cow, 'nursing' can refer to its milk. For a donkey, it must mean the foal is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the seller said, 'I am selling you a nursing donkey' or 'a nursing cow.' With a cow, we can say the buyer wants it for its milk. But with a donkey, why would he mention nursing? Learn from this that he meant 'the donkey and its young.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. He gives a middle case: the seller did not say 'and its young,' but he did say 'nursing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'nursing' means different things for the two animals. Cow's milk is useful, so 'nursing' may just describe the cow as a milk cow. Nobody buys a donkey for its milk, so for a donkey the word only makes sense if the nursing foal is part of the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Nursing (an animal that is feeding its young)
It makes sense with... (introduces the easy case before the hard one)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'nursing' includes the young in a donkey sale but not in a cow sale, because only a cow's milk has value.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is where he said to him: 'A nursing donkey'
or 'a nursing cow I am selling you.'
It makes sense with a cow:
one can say he wants it for its milk.
But a donkey, what is he telling him?
phrases.notes: Nobody buys a donkey for its milk, so why mention that it is nursing?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ – הִיא וּבְנָהּ קָאָמַר לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: Learn from this: he is telling him 'it and its young.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ חֲמוֹר מְנִיקָה וּפָרָה מְנִיקָה אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma by giving a middle case that the challenge had not considered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a case between the two options in the dilemma: the seller said 'nursing' without saying 'and its young.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller either clearly said 'and its young' or said nothing, so both animals should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said 'nursing.' For a cow this can refer to its milk, but for a donkey it can only mean the foal is included.

steps.title: Why is a foal called סייח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks, as a side point, why a donkey foal is called סייח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it called a 'סייח'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside to ask about the meaning of the word סייח. It is setting up a short answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is not part of the legal discussion. It is a side question about the word the משנה used for a donkey foal.

phrases.english: And why does it call it a 'foal'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ סְיָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the legal discussion briefly to explain a word from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the name סייח comes from

steps.title: It follows pleasant talk
steps.stepSummary: A foal is called סייח because it follows after pleasant talk, called סיחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it walks after pleasant talk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name comes from סיחה, meaning talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young foal will follow you if you speak to it gently, so its name, סייח, is connected to the word סיחה, pleasant talk.

phrases.english: Because it walks after pleasant talk.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמְּהַלֵּךְ אַחַר סִיחָה נָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side question about the word סייח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name סייח comes from סיחה, because the foal follows gentle talk.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן begins explaining a פסוק about 'the המושלים'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמן, quoting רבי יוחנן, asks what the פסוק 'Therefore the המושלים say' means. The explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמן said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'Therefore the המושלים say...'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It opens with a question about a פסוק, and the גמרא is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new teaching of אגדה, not part of the law of selling. The opening 'what is written' means the פסוק is about to be read with a deeper meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (opens an explanation of a פסוק)
Those who speak in parables, or those who rule
And so on (the rest of the פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'Therefore those who speak in parables say, etc.'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the law of selling and begins a new teaching on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens רבי יוחנן's explanation of the פסוק 'Therefore the המושלים say.' The explanation itself comes next.

steps.title: Those who rule their inclination weigh the world's true account
steps.stepSummary: המושלים are people who control their יצר. 'Come to חשבון' means: let us weigh the real cost of a מצוה against its reward, and the gain of an עבירה against its loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The ones who rule' means people who rule over their inclination. 'Come to חשבון' means: come, let us make the world's calculation. Weigh what you lose by doing a מצוה against the reward you get for it. Weigh what you gain from a sin against what you lose because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the explanation that step 15 promised. It reads the first words of the פסוק as a lesson about self-control and honest calculation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word המושלים normally means 'those who speak in parables,' but here it is read as 'those who rule,' meaning people who rule over themselves. The city name חשבון is read as the word for 'calculation.' The lesson is that a wise person looks at the full picture: a מצוה may cost something now, but its reward is far bigger, while a sin may feel good now, but its loss is far bigger.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who rule over their (evil) inclination
A calculation or account; also the name of סיחון's city
The loss or cost you take on by doing a מצוה
The gain or pleasure you get from a sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'calculation' idea is the key that unlocks the whole דרשה. Each later phrase is read as either the reward for making this calculation or the punishment for refusing to make it.

phrases.english: "The ones who rule": these are the people who rule over their inclination.
phrases.notes: In the פסוק (במדבר 21:27) this word usually means 'those who tell parables.' The גמרא reads it as 'those who rule.'

phrases.english: "Come to Heshbon":
phrases.notes: חשבון is a city name, but the word also means 'calculation.' The דרשה is built on that double meaning.

phrases.english: come and let us calculate the account of the world:
the loss of doing a מצוה, weighed against its reward,
and the gain of a sin, weighed against its loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמֹּשְׁלִים – אֵלּוּ הַמּוֹשְׁלִים בְּיִצְרָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the explanation that step 15 promised for the פסוק 'Therefore the המושלים say.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the פסוק 'Therefore the המושלים say, come to חשבון' means (asked in step 15).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It speaks about people who rule over their יצר and weigh the cost of מצוות against their reward, and the gain of sins against their loss.

steps.title: The reward for making the calculation
steps.stepSummary: Someone who makes this honest calculation is built up in עולם הזה and established in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let it be built and established' means: if you make this calculation, you will be built up in this world and firmly set up in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the פסוק. The next words describe the reward for a person who makes the calculation from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two verbs, 'built' and 'established.' The גמרא gives each one its own world: 'built' is in עולם הזה, and 'established' is in עולם הבא. So the honest calculator gains in both worlds.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be built and established

phrases.english: "Let it be built and established":
if you do this (make this calculation),
you will be built up in this world
and you will be established for the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּבָּנֶה וְתִכּוֹנֵן – אִם אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the דרשה by describing the reward for the person from step 16 who makes the calculation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who weighs the cost and reward of מצוות and sins is built up in עולם הזה and established in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The one who chases desire like a young donkey gets burned
steps.stepSummary: 'עיר סיחון' is read as a young donkey (עייר) that follows pleasant talk (סיחה). The next פסוק says fire goes out from those who calculate and burns those who do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The city of סיחון' means: if a person makes himself like this young donkey that follows after sweet talk, what is written right after? 'For a fire went out from חשבון.' A fire will come out from those who calculate and burn up those who do not calculate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now describes the opposite type of person, someone who just follows his desires. It shows from the next פסוק what happens to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עיר (city) is read as עַיִר (young donkey), and סיחון is read as סיחה (pleasant talk). This ties back to step 14, where a foal was described as following sweet talk. Such a person never stops to calculate, and the 'fire from חשבון' is read as a fire coming from the people who do calculate and burning those who do not.

keyTerms.meaning: A young donkey; here a wordplay on עִיר, 'city'
Those who calculate (the account of their deeds)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about an actual city or a real donkey. The גמרא is playing on the sounds of the words to teach a lesson about people who follow their desires without thinking.

phrases.english: "The city of Sihon":
phrases.notes: עיר ('city') is read as עַיִר ('young donkey'), and סיחון is read as סיחה ('pleasant talk').

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּעַיִר זֶה,
phrases.english: if a person makes himself like this young donkey
that follows after pleasant talk,
phrases.notes: This points back to step 14, where a foal is called סייח because it follows sweet talk.

phrases.english: what is written after it?
"For a fire went out from Heshbon, etc.":
a fire will go out from those who calculate,
and it will consume those who do not calculate.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִיר סִיחוֹן – אִם מֵשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּעַיִר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 17: after the reward of the calculator comes the punishment of the one who follows his desires.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who follows his desires without calculating is consumed by a fire that comes from those who do calculate.

steps.title: A flame from the righteous burns the one who follows his inclination
steps.stepSummary: 'A flame from the city of סיחון' means from the righteous, who are called שיחין (trees). 'It consumed ער מואב' refers to one who follows his יצר like a young donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a flame from the city of סיחון' means from the city of the צדיקים, who are called 'trees.' 'It consumed ער of מואב' means the person who follows his inclination, like this young donkey that follows after pleasant talk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with the second half of the same פסוק. It explains where the flame comes from and whom it burns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סיחון is now read as שיחין, a name for the צדיקים, so the flame comes from the righteous. ער is read like עַיִר again, so the victim is the person who chases his יצר. This repeats the idea of step 18: those who calculate burn up those who do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Trees or bushes; here a name for the צדיקים
One who follows after his inclination

phrases.english: "And a flame from the city of Sihon":
from the city of the righteous, who are called "trees."
phrases.notes: שיחין sounds like סיחון, so the גמרא reads the name as pointing to the righteous.

phrases.english: "It consumed Ar of Moab":
this is one who follows after his inclination,

phrases.aramaic: כְּעַיִר זֶה שֶׁמְּהַלֵּךְ אַחַר סִיחָה נָאָה.
phrases.english: like this young donkey that follows after pleasant talk.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֶהָבָה מִקִּרְיַת סִיחֹן – מִקִּרְיַת צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק as step 18 and repeats its idea through new wordplays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flame comes from the צדיקים and consumes the one who follows his יצר.

steps.title: The arrogant fall into גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: 'The lords of the high places of ארנון' are the arrogant. A teaching of מר supports this: every arrogant person falls into גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The lords of the high places of ארנון' are the arrogant people, as מר said: any person who has arrogance in him falls into גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the end of the פסוק as speaking about arrogant people. It backs this up with a known teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'High places' hints at people who hold themselves high, meaning the arrogant. The quote 'דאמר מר' shows why the פסוק counts them among those burned: arrogance itself leads a person to גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (introducing a known teaching)
The place of punishment after death

phrases.english: "The lords of the high places of Arnon":
these are the arrogant,
as the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ,
phrases.english: any person who has arrogance in him
falls into Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלֵי בָּמוֹת אַרְנֹן – אֵלּוּ גַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ, דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same פסוק, adding the arrogant to the list of those consumed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arrogant are among those consumed, since every arrogant person falls into גיהנם.

steps.title: The wicked deny there is a Judge, and ה׳ says wait for judgment
steps.stepSummary: ונירם is read as the רשע saying 'there is no One on high' and 'the world's account is lost.' עד דיבון is read as הקדוש ברוך הוא answering: wait until judgment comes. The next phrase, ונשים, begins here and its explanation continues on the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ונירם' means: the wicked man says, 'There is no One on high.' 'חשבון is lost' means: the world's account is lost. 'Until דיבון' means: הקדוש ברוך הוא says, 'Wait until judgment comes.' 'And we laid waste'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק (במדבר 21:30) and reads it as a conversation: the רשע denies any accounting, and ה׳ answers him. The last words start the next phrase, which is explained after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ונירם is split into אין רם, 'there is none on high,' meaning the רשע denies there is a God who judges. 'חשבון is lost' becomes his claim that there is no accounting for deeds, which is the exact opposite of the calculation in step 16. דיבון is read as יבוא דין, 'judgment will come,' which is ה׳'s answer: the reckoning is delayed, not cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We shot at them'; read here as אֵין רָם, 'there is none on high'
A place name; read as יָבֹא דִּין, 'judgment will come'

steps.whatToRemember: The whole דרשה is about the 'account of the world.' The wise rule their יצר and calculate, and they are built up in both worlds. Those who chase desire, the arrogant, and the רשע who says there is no account will all face judgment in the end.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Heshbon is lost' is the claim of the רשע, not the conclusion of the גמרא‎. ה׳'s answer, 'wait until judgment comes,' shows that his claim is wrong.

phrases.english: "And we shot at them":
phrases.notes: במדבר 21:30. The word is split up and read as אין רם, 'there is none on high.'

phrases.english: the wicked man says: there is no One on high.
"Heshbon is lost":
the account of the world is lost.
"Until Dibon":
The Holy One, Blessed be He, says:
wait until judgment comes.
"And we laid waste"

steps.triggerLanguage: וַנִּירָם – אָמַר רָשָׁע: אֵין רָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק and shows the opposite of step 16: the רשע who denies any accounting at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רשע claims there is no Judge and no accounting, and הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that judgment will surely come.
